cross_industry.statement: A chipmaker said its main foundry partner will raise wafer prices 10% next year.
A bank's CFO said loan growth would be solid this year.
An automaker recalled 1.2 million vehicles over a brake defect.
A rival of the drug maker received FDA approval for a competing drug.
A cloud provider said it signed a multi-year deal with a large retailer; no value was disclosed.
Shares of the retailer rose 12% after its earnings report.
A magazine named the retailer one of the best places to work.
Industry data show global smartphone shipments fell 4% in the second quarter.
An oil major's CEO said he expects oil prices to average $70 a barrel next year.
A telecom operator's spokesperson declined to comment on reports it may sell its tower business.
The software company held its annual user conference with 20,000 attendees.
A steelmaker took a $300 million impairment on an idle plant.

questions.question: Will the chipmaker's main foundry partner raise wafer prices by the end of 2026? (the foundry is not a covered company)
What will global smartphone shipments be in calendar 2026?
What will the airline's FY2026 fuel cost per available seat mile be?
Will the competition regulator approve the telecom operator's merger with its rival by mid-2027?
What will the retailer's fourth-quarter same-store sales growth be?
Will the bank complete its $2 billion buyback by the end of the year?
What will the software company's FY2027 annual recurring revenue be?
Will the steelmaker's CEO be replaced by 2027?
Will the drug maker sign the reported $12 billion acquisition within 18 months?
How much will the chipmaker's revenue grow over the next five years?
